bidding_conventions/bart.name: BART
bidding_conventions/bart.summary:
After 1♥ or 1♠, a forcing 1NT and opener's 2♣, responder's 2♦ is artificial,
covering several stronger hands (a good club raise, a good preference,
diamonds) that need room.

bidding_conventions/benjamin_2d.name: Benjamin 2♦
bidding_conventions/benjamin_2d.summary:
Openings in which 2♣ shows a strong two in any suit, 2♦ is the game-forcing
hand, and 2♥ and 2♠ are weak twos, so there is no weak 2♦.

bidding_conventions/bergen_raises.name: Bergen raises
bidding_conventions/bergen_raises.summary:
Over partner's 1♥ or 1♠, responder's jumps to 3♣ and 3♦ show four-card
raises of different strength (usually 3♣ constructive, 3♦ limit) and 3M is
preemptive, so opener knows the fit and strength at once.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/blackwood.name: Blackwood
bidding_conventions/blackwood.summary:
Once a trump suit is agreed, 4NT asks how many aces partner holds: 5♣ none
or four, 5♦ one, 5♥ two, 5♠ three. 5NT then asks for kings the same way.

bidding_conventions/checkback.name: Checkback
bidding_conventions/checkback.summary:
Played instead of NMF: after opener's notrump rebid, a fixed suit (usually
2♣) asks about support and majors, whichever minor was bid.

bidding_conventions/control_bids.name: Control (Cue) Bids
bidding_conventions/control_bids.summary:
With a trump suit agreed and slam possible, bidding a new suit below game
shows a control there (an ace or void, and in many styles a king or
singleton), so the partnership can find out whether a suit is unguarded
before asking for keycards.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/depo.name: DEPO
bidding_conventions/depo.summary:
Played instead of DOPI: when they interfere over a keycard ask, double shows
an even number of keycards and pass an odd number.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi.name: DOPI and ROPI
bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi.summary:
When the opponents interfere over a keycard ask, double shows no keycards
(or none of the first step) and pass shows one (DOPI); after they double,
redouble shows none and pass one (ROPI). The next steps continue.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
Slam Bidding: Dealing with Interference Over Ace-Asking Bids

bidding_conventions/drury.name: Drury
bidding_conventions/drury.summary:
By a passed hand over partner's third- or fourth-seat 1♥ or 1♠, 2♣ asks
whether opener has a full opening, with a fit for the major. In the original
form opener's 2♦ shows a light opening; Reverse Drury swaps opener's
replies.

bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood.name: Exclusion Blackwood
bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood.summary:
A jump to the five level in a new suit after agreeing trumps shows a void
there and asks for keycards outside it, so the ace in the void suit does not
count.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/flannery.name: Flannery 2♦
bidding_conventions/flannery.summary:
An opening 2♦ showing a minimum opening with five hearts and four spades, so
responder can find a spade fit without opener having to reverse or rebid
awkwardly.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/forcing_1nt.name: Forcing 1NT
bidding_conventions/forcing_1nt.summary:
Over partner's 1♥ or 1♠, responder's 1NT is forcing for one round, covering
a wide range of hands including invitational ones; opener must bid again, on
a three-card minor if need be.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing.name: Fourth Suit Forcing
bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing.summary:
When three suits have been bid, responder's bid of the fourth suit is
artificial and forcing (for one round, or to game by agreement), asking
opener to describe the hand further.

bidding_conventions/french_2d.name: French 2♦
bidding_conventions/french_2d.summary:
An opening 2♦ with an artificial meaning in the French style; details vary
by partnership, so the card's notes say which.

bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt.name: Gambling 3NT
bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt.summary:
An opening 3NT showing a long, solid minor with little outside. Partner
passes with stoppers in the other suits, and otherwise runs to four or five
of the minor.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
NT Auctions: Trick-Showing NT Bids - Gambling 3NT and More

bidding_conventions/gazzilli.name: Gazzilli
bidding_conventions/gazzilli.summary:
After 1♥ or 1♠ and a 1NT response, opener's 2♣ is artificial: either natural
clubs or any strong hand. Responder's 2♦ asks, letting opener show strong
hands at the two level.

bidding_conventions/gerber.name: Gerber
bidding_conventions/gerber.summary:
A jump to 4♣ over partner's notrump asks for aces, with steps answering as
for Blackwood (4♦ none or four, 4♥ one, and so on), leaving 4NT as a natural
raise.

bidding_conventions/grand_slam_force.name: Grand slam force
bidding_conventions/grand_slam_force.summary:
A jump to 5NT (not after a keycard ask) asks partner to bid the grand slam
in the agreed suit holding two of the top three trump honours.

bidding_conventions/help_suit_game_try.name: Help Suit Game Try
bidding_conventions/help_suit_game_try.summary:
After a major-suit raise, opener's new suit is a game try asking for help
there: responder bids game with honours or shortness in that suit and signs
off without.

bidding_conventions/impossible_2s.name: Impossible 2♠
bidding_conventions/impossible_2s.summary:
After 1♥–1NT–2♣ or 2♦, responder's 2♠ cannot be natural, so it shows a good
raise of opener's minor, forcing to three of it.

bidding_conventions/ingberman.name: Ingberman 2NT
bidding_conventions/ingberman.summary:
After opener reverses, responder's 2NT relays to 3♣ to show a weak hand, so
other bids by responder show values.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/inverted_minors.name: Inverted Minor Raises
bidding_conventions/inverted_minors.summary:
Over partner's 1♣ or 1♦, the single raise is strong (invitational or better,
forcing one round) and the jump raise is weak, the reverse of the natural
meanings. It usually denies a four-card major.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
Inverted Minors and 1D-2C Auctions with Structure

bidding_conventions/jacoby_2nt.name: Jacoby 2NT
bidding_conventions/jacoby_2nt.summary:
Over partner's 1♥ or 1♠, responder's 2NT shows four or more trumps and game-
forcing values. Opener's rebid describes the hand: a short suit at the three
level, a good second suit at the four level, or strength by 3M, 3NT or 4M.

bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers.name: Jacoby Transfers

see.title: NT Auctions: Opponents' Doubles of Our Stayman and Transfers

bidding_conventions/kickback.name: Kickback
bidding_conventions/kickback.summary:
A keycard ask in the suit above trumps instead of 4NT: 4♦ with clubs as
trumps, 4♥ with diamonds, 4♠ with hearts, and 4NT with spades. The answers
then never take the auction past five of the trump suit.

bidding_conventions/kokish.name: Kokish relay
bidding_conventions/kokish.summary:
After 2♣–2♦, opener's 2♥ is a relay: either hearts or a strong balanced
hand. Responder must bid 2♠, and opener's next bid says which, which keeps
the strong 2NT rebid out of the way.

bidding_conventions/kokish_game_tries.name: Kokish game tries
bidding_conventions/kokish_game_tries.summary:
A structure of game tries after a major-suit raise that uses the next step
as a relay, so opener can make several kinds of try.

bidding_conventions/lars_multi.name: Lars Multi 2♦
bidding_conventions/lars_multi.summary: A Multi 2♦ that shows a weak two in either major or a 20–21 balanced hand.

bidding_conventions/last_train.name: Last Train
bidding_conventions/last_train.summary:
When the only bid left between a fit and game in the agreed major is one
step below it, that bid is a general slam try rather than showing anything
in its suit.

see.title: Slam Bidding: Last Train Slam Try

bidding_conventions/mccabe.name: McCabe adjunct
bidding_conventions/mccabe.summary:
After partner's weak two is doubled, responder's new suits and 2NT say what
to lead rather than show length, so the partnership can compete and direct
the defence at once.

bidding_conventions/mini_roman_2d.name: Mini-Roman 2♦
bidding_conventions/mini_roman_2d.summary:
An opening 2♦ showing a three-suited hand (4-4-4-1 or 5-4-4-0) of opening
strength; responder bids the cheapest suit to play or 2NT to ask for the
short suit.

bidding_conventions/minor_suit_stayman.name: Minor Suit Stayman
bidding_conventions/minor_suit_stayman.summary:
Over partner's 1NT (or 2NT), a bid, usually 2♠, asks opener for a four-card
minor, for responder with both minors and slam interest or a hand looking
for a minor-suit game.

bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers.name: Minor-Suit Transfers over 1NT
bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers.summary:
Over partner's 1NT, responder's 2♠ and 2NT (or 3♣) are transfers or relays
to the minors, so a long minor can be shown weak to play or strong with slam
interest.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/minorwood.name: Minorwood
bidding_conventions/minorwood.summary:
With a minor agreed, four of that minor asks for keycards instead of 4NT,
keeping the answers low enough to stop in five of the minor.

bidding_conventions/modified_jacoby_2nt.name: Modified Jacoby 2NT
bidding_conventions/modified_jacoby_2nt.summary:
Played instead of standard Jacoby 2NT: responder's 2NT is the same raise,
but opener's rebids are rearranged, usually so that 3♣ shows a minimum and
responder can then ask for shortness.

bidding_conventions/muiderberg.name: Muiderberg twos
bidding_conventions/muiderberg.summary:
Openings of 2♥ and 2♠ that show five cards in the major and four or more in
a minor, with less than an opening bid.

bidding_conventions/multi_2d.name: Multi 2♦
bidding_conventions/multi_2d.summary:
An opening 2♦ that shows a weak two in either major, or one of a few strong
hands. Responder bids to cater for either major, and opener's rebid resolves
which.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/namyats.name: Namyats
bidding_conventions/namyats.summary:
Openings of 4♣ and 4♦ show a strong four-level preempt in hearts and spades
respectively, so a direct 4♥ or 4♠ opening is weaker.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing.name: New Minor Forcing
bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing.summary:
After opener's 1NT rebid, responder's bid of the unbid minor is artificial
and forcing, asking opener about three-card support for responder's major or
a four-card other major.

bidding_conventions/ogust.name: Ogust
bidding_conventions/ogust.summary:
After partner's weak two, responder's 2NT asks about the hand in steps: 3♣
bad hand bad suit, 3♦ bad hand good suit, 3♥ good hand bad suit, 3♠ good
hand good suit, 3NT a solid suit.

bidding_conventions/over_splinters.name: Over-splinters
bidding_conventions/over_splinters.summary:
A jump one level beyond a normal splinter, used when the normal splinter bid
has another meaning, to show shortness and a fit.

bidding_conventions/pick_a_slam_5nt.name: Pick-a-slam 5NT
bidding_conventions/pick_a_slam_5nt.summary:
A 5NT bid, not after a keycard ask, asks partner to choose among several
possible slams, usually in notrump or in a suit partner prefers.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/picture_3nt.name: 1M–3NT picture raise
bidding_conventions/picture_3nt.summary:
Over partner's 1♥ or 1♠, responder's 3NT is a game-forcing raise with a
balanced hand and good trumps, better than a direct raise to four.

bidding_conventions/polish_two_suiters.name: Polish two-suiters
bidding_conventions/polish_two_suiters.summary:
Weak openings at the two level that show two-suited hands, with the second
suit unknown or limited, as used in Polish Club.

bidding_conventions/precision_2d.name: Precision 2♦
bidding_conventions/precision_2d.summary:
In Precision, an opening 2♦ shows a limited opening short in diamonds,
usually 4-4-1-4 or 4-4-0-5 with 11-15 points.

bidding_conventions/preempt_keycard.name: Keycard over preempts
bidding_conventions/preempt_keycard.summary:
After partner's preempt, an agreed bid (often 4♣) asks for keycards in
partner's suit, since 4NT would take the auction too high.

bidding_conventions/puppet_stayman.name: Puppet Stayman
bidding_conventions/puppet_stayman.summary:
A form of Stayman, usually over 2NT, that finds five-card majors as well as
four-card ones: 3♣ asks, opener shows a five-card major directly or bids 3♦
with a four-card major, and responder then bids the major responder does
not hold.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
NT Auctions: Puppet Stayman and 5-Card Stayman

bidding_conventions/range_stayman.name: Range Stayman
bidding_conventions/range_stayman.summary:
Over partner's 1NT, a bid (often 2♠, or 2♣ then 2♠) asks whether opener is
minimum or maximum, for responder with an invitation to 2NT or a minor-suit
hand.

see.title: NT and Balancing Auctions: Range Stayman

bidding_conventions/reverse_bergen_raise.name: Reverse Bergen raises
bidding_conventions/reverse_bergen_raise.summary:
Played instead of Bergen raises: the same four-card raises with the meanings
of 3♣ and 3♦ swapped.

bidding_conventions/reverse_bids.name: Reverse Bids
bidding_conventions/reverse_bids.summary:
Opener's rebid in a new suit higher than the first, at the two level, shows
extra strength and a longer first suit; it is forcing for one round in most
styles.

bidding_conventions/reverse_drury.name: Reverse Drury
bidding_conventions/reverse_drury.summary:
By a passed hand over partner's third- or fourth-seat 1♥ or 1♠, 2♣ shows a
limit raise with three or more trumps. Opener rebids two of the major with a
light opening; other bids show a full one.

bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery.name: Reverse Flannery
bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery.summary:
An opening of 2♥ (or 2♦) showing five or more spades and four or more hearts
with less than an opening, a two-suited preempt in the majors.

bidding_conventions/roman_keycard.name: Roman Keycard
bidding_conventions/roman_keycard.summary:
4NT asks for five keycards, the four aces and the trump king. 1430 answers
5♣ one or four, 5♦ three or none, 5♥ two without the trump queen, 5♠ two
with it; 0314 swaps 5♣ and 5♦. The next step asks for the trump queen.

bidding_conventions/roudi.name: Roudi
bidding_conventions/roudi.summary:
A checkback used in Acol and similar systems after opener's 1NT rebid, with
2♣ asking about support and strength.

bidding_conventions/semi_forcing_1nt.name: Semi-forcing 1NT
bidding_conventions/semi_forcing_1nt.summary:
Played instead of the forcing 1NT: responder's 1NT over a major is forcing
only if opener has more than a minimum, so opener may pass with a balanced
minimum.

see.title: 2 over 1 Game Forcing: Responder's Rebids after 1NT Semi-Forcing Response

bidding_conventions/serious_3nt.name: Serious 3NT
bidding_conventions/serious_3nt.summary:
In a game-forcing auction with a major agreed at the three level, 3NT is
artificial and says whether the bidder is serious about slam (serious or
non-serious by agreement), before control bids begin.

bidding_conventions/six_key_rkcb.name: Six-key Roman Keycard
bidding_conventions/six_key_rkcb.summary:
Roman Keycard with two trump suits: six keycards, the four aces and both
trump kings, plus both trump queens, when the partnership has a fit in two
suits.

bidding_conventions/smolen.name: Smolen
bidding_conventions/smolen.summary:
After 1NT–2♣–2♦, responder with five cards in one major, four in the other
and game values jumps to three of the four-card major, so the strong hand
becomes declarer in a 5-3 fit.

see.title: Smolen and 5/5 Majors After a 2NT Opening

bidding_conventions/soloway.name: Soloway jump shifts
bidding_conventions/soloway.summary:
Responder's jump shifts are strong and describe the hand by type: a one-
suiter, a fit for opener, or a balanced hand, as GIB plays them.

bidding_conventions/spiral.name: Spiral
bidding_conventions/spiral.summary:
A relay that asks about trump length and quality in steps once a fit is
found, so the asker can judge game or slam from how good the trumps are.

see.title: Fits and More: 2NT Trump Suit Game Try - Spiral

bidding_conventions/splinters.name: Splinters
bidding_conventions/splinters.summary:
A double jump in a new suit, by responder or by opener, shows a singleton or
void there and a fit with game values, so partner can judge slam by how well
the hands fit.

see.title: Slam Bidding: Splinter Bids by Responder

bidding_conventions/stayman.name: Stayman
bidding_conventions/stayman.summary:
Over partner's 1NT, 2♣ asks opener for a four-card major: 2♦ denies one, 2♥
or 2♠ shows it. Responder uses it to find a 4-4 major fit with invitational
or better values; Garbage Stayman uses it weak, planning to pass any reply.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/strong_2c.name: Strong 2♣
bidding_conventions/strong_2c.summary:
An opening 2♣, artificial and forcing, for the strongest hands: game-forcing
or nearly so, balanced or not. Responder usually bids 2♦ to wait, and opener
then describes the hand.

bidding_conventions/super_accept.name: Super-Accepting a Transfer
bidding_conventions/super_accept.summary:
After partner's transfer over 1NT, opener with four-card support and a
maximum bids above the two-level completion to say so, and responder can bid
a thin game.

bidding_conventions/tislevoll.name: Tislevoll slam try
bidding_conventions/tislevoll.summary:
After partner opens a major and the opponents preempt, responder's 4♣ and 4♦
are slam tries in partner's major that show or deny a control in the
opponents' suit.

bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh.name: Transfer Walsh
bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh.summary:
Over partner's 1♣, responder's 1♦ and 1♥ are transfers to the next suit,
showing four or more cards in it, and 1♠ denies a four-card major. Opener
can accept the transfer, so the 1♣ hand often declares.

bidding_conventions/transfers_after_doub.name: Transfers after a takeout double
bidding_conventions/transfers_after_doub.summary:
After partner's opening is doubled for takeout, responder's new-suit bids
are transfers to the next suit, so opener can accept or show a fit and
responder can describe more hands.

bidding_conventions/two_heart_bust.name: 2♥ bust over 2♣
bidding_conventions/two_heart_bust.summary:
After 2♣–2♦ and opener's natural rebid, a cheapest-suit reply shows a very
weak hand, so opener knows when to stop short of game. The Parrish form uses
2♥ as the bust in some auctions.

bidding_conventions/two_over_one.name: 2/1 Game Force
bidding_conventions/two_over_one.summary:
After a one-level opening, responder's new suit at the two level, without
jumping and by an unpassed hand, forces to game. The auction can then go
slowly, with room to describe both hands.

see.title: 2 over 1 Game Forcing: Modern Bridge Standard

bidding_conventions/two_way_drury.name: Two-way Drury
bidding_conventions/two_way_drury.summary:
Played instead of Drury: a passed hand's 2♣ and 2♦ over partner's third- or
fourth-seat major both show limit raises, split by trump length (usually 2♣
three trumps, 2♦ four).

bidding_conventions/two_way_game_tries.name: Two-way game tries
bidding_conventions/two_way_game_tries.summary:
After a major raise, opener's 2NT (or the next step) is a relay for one kind
of game try and new suits are another, so opener can make short-suit and
long-suit tries.

bidding_conventions/two_way_nmf.name: Two-way new minor forcing
bidding_conventions/two_way_nmf.summary:
Played instead of NMF: after opener's 1NT rebid, responder's 2♣ relays to 2♦
(to sign off or invite) and 2♦ is game forcing.

see.title: Two-Way New Minor Forcing aka xyNT
2-Way New Minor Forcing and Wolff Signoff

bidding_conventions/walsh.name: Walsh
bidding_conventions/walsh.summary:
Over partner's 1♣, responder with a weak or moderate hand bids a four-card
major ahead of longer diamonds, so opener can rebid 1NT with any balanced
hand knowing no 4-4 major fit is lost.

see.title: Thinking and Responding: Walsh and Extended Walsh

bidding_conventions/weak_2s.name: Weak Twos
bidding_conventions/weak_2s.summary:
An opening 2♦, 2♥ or 2♠ shows a good six-card suit and less than an opening
bid, as a preempt. Responder's 2NT usually asks for more, and a raise
continues the preempt.

bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts.name: Weak jump shifts
bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts.summary:
Responder's jump in a new suit over partner's one-level opening shows a long
suit and a weak hand, rather than a strong one.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
Thinking and Responding: Jump Shifts After 1-Level Openings - Weak and Invitational

bidding_conventions/western_cuebid.name: Western cue bid
bidding_conventions/western_cuebid.summary:
A cue bid of the opponents' suit when looking for 3NT asks partner to bid
notrump with a stopper in that suit.

bidding_conventions/wilkosz.name: Wilkosz 2♦
bidding_conventions/wilkosz.summary:
An opening 2♦ showing a weak two-suited hand with at least five cards in
each of two suits, one of them a major.

bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff.name: Wolff signoff
bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff.summary:
After opener's 2NT rebid (1m–1M–2NT), responder's 3♣ forces opener to bid
3♦, so responder can sign off in a suit or show weaker hands; other three-
level bids force.

see.title: 2-Way New Minor Forcing and Wolff Signoff

bidding_conventions/xyz.name: XYZ
bidding_conventions/xyz.summary:
After any three one-level bids, responder's 2♣ relays to 2♦ and 2♦ is game
forcing, extending two-way checkback to every such auction.

competitive_bidding/anti_lead_directing_.name: Anti-lead-directing doubles
competitive_bidding/anti_lead_directing_.summary:
When a lead-directing double of an artificial bid is expected, a double asks
partner not to lead that suit, and a pass says nothing.

competitive_bidding/bromad.name: BROMAD
competitive_bidding/bromad.summary:
Bergen raises used over the opponents' takeout double of partner's major
(Bergen Raises Over Major Doubles), with the structure adjusted for the
double.

competitive_bidding/cappelletti.name: Cappelletti over 1NT
competitive_bidding/cappelletti.summary:
Over their 1NT: double is for penalty, 2♣ shows a one-suited hand, 2♦ both
majors, 2♥ and 2♠ that major and a minor, 2NT both minors.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/collante.name: Collante
competitive_bidding/collante.summary:
After partner's 1♣ and their 1♦ (or 1♦ and 1♥), a double shows four cards in
the next suit up and a bid of it shows five or more.

competitive_bidding/crash.name: CRASH
competitive_bidding/crash.summary:
A defence to a strong 1♣ opening: overcalls show two-suited hands by colour,
rank and shape (CRASH: Colour, RAnk, SHape).

competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt.name: Defending against 1NT
competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt.summary:
An agreement on what overcalls and doubles of the opponents' 1NT mean,
usually a system that shows two-suited hands at the two level. The card
names which one, against strong and weak notrumps.

competitive_bidding/dont.name: DONT
competitive_bidding/dont.summary:
Over their strong 1NT: double shows one long suit (partner relays 2♣); 2♣
and 2♦ show that suit and a higher one; 2♥ both majors; 2♠ six or more
spades.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/equal_level_conversi.name: Equal level conversion
competitive_bidding/equal_level_conversi.summary:
After a takeout double and partner's forced response, the doubler's bid of
another suit at the same level shows a two-suited hand without extra
strength, rather than a strong one.

competitive_bidding/exit_transfers.name: Exit transfers
competitive_bidding/exit_transfers.summary:
When the opponents double partner's 1NT, redouble and suit bids are
transfers to the next suit to escape, and pass forces a redouble for two-
suited runouts.

competitive_bidding/fit_showing_jumps.name: Fit-showing jumps
competitive_bidding/fit_showing_jumps.summary:
In competition, a jump in a new suit shows a good suit there and a fit for
partner, so partner can judge how the hands fit.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/forcing_pass.name: Forcing pass
competitive_bidding/forcing_pass.summary:
When the partnership has shown game-invitational or better values and an
opponent bids, a pass is forcing: it asks partner to double or bid, and
shows interest in continuing.

competitive_bidding/ghestem.name: Ghestem
competitive_bidding/ghestem.summary:
Played instead of Michaels and the Unusual 2NT: 2NT, a cue bid and a jump
cue bid each show a specific pair of suits.

competitive_bidding/good_bad_2nt.name: Good/bad 2NT
competitive_bidding/good_bad_2nt.summary:
In a competitive auction where the opponents have just bid at the two level,
2NT is artificial and shows a weak hand that wants to compete to the three
level; bidding the three level directly is stronger.

competitive_bidding/jordan_2nt.name: Jordan 2NT
competitive_bidding/jordan_2nt.summary:
After partner's opening is doubled for takeout, responder's 2NT shows a
limit raise or better in partner's suit, leaving the direct raises weak.

competitive_bidding/landy.name: Landy
competitive_bidding/landy.summary: Over their 1NT, 2♣ shows both majors; other overcalls are natural.

competitive_bidding/lead_directing_doubl.name: Lead-directing doubles
competitive_bidding/lead_directing_doubl.summary:
A double of an artificial bid (a cue bid, Stayman, a transfer, a response to
an ace ask) or of a slam asks partner to lead that suit, or a specific
unusual suit.

competitive_bidding/leaping_michaels.name: Leaping Michaels
competitive_bidding/leaping_michaels.summary:
Over their weak two, a jump to four of a minor shows that minor and the
other major (or both majors over a minor), five-five with game values.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/lebensohl.name: Lebensohl
competitive_bidding/lebensohl.summary:
When they overcall partner's 1NT, responder's 2NT is a relay to 3♣: the two-
step route shows a weaker or different hand from a direct bid, and whether
responder cue-bids fast or slow tells whether a stopper is held.

see.title: NT Bidding: Responding to 1NT in Competition - Lebensohl

competitive_bidding/mathe.name: Mathe
competitive_bidding/mathe.summary:
A defence to a strong 1♣ opening: double shows the majors, 1NT the minors,
and suit bids are natural.

see.title: Competitive Bidding: Bidding Over Strong 2C (and 1C) Openings - Mathe

competitive_bidding/maximal_doubles.name: Maximal doubles
competitive_bidding/maximal_doubles.summary:
When the opponents have competed to the three level just below your suit, a
double is a game try rather than penalty, since there is no room for another
try.

see.title: Non-Takeout Doubles: Card-Showing, Maximal, Penalty, Lead-Directing

competitive_bidding/meckwell.name: Meckwell over 1NT
competitive_bidding/meckwell.summary:
Over their 1NT: double shows a one-suited minor or both majors; 2♣ and 2♦
show that minor and a major; 2♥ and 2♠ are natural; 2NT shows both minors.

competitive_bidding/michaels_unusual.name: Michaels & Unusual 2NT

competitive_bidding/mitchell_stayman.name: Mitchell Stayman
competitive_bidding/mitchell_stayman.summary:
After partner's minor opening and their 1NT overcall, responder's 2♣ shows
both majors (five-four) with modest values, and opener chooses.

competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti.name: Modified Cappelletti
competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti.summary:
Played instead of Cappelletti: over their 1NT, 2♣ shows a one-suited minor
or a major and a minor, and 2♥ and 2♠ are natural one-suiters.

competitive_bidding/multi_landy.name: Landy and Multi-Landy over 1NT
competitive_bidding/multi_landy.summary:
Over their 1NT: double shows a four-card major and a longer minor, 2♣ both
majors, 2♦ one long major, and 2♥ and 2♠ that major with a minor.

competitive_bidding/negative_doubles.name: Negative Doubles
competitive_bidding/negative_doubles.summary:
After partner opens and the next player overcalls, responder's double is for
takeout, usually showing the unbid major or majors, so responder can compete
without a long suit or a fit.

competitive_bidding/non_leaping_michaels.name: Non-leaping Michaels
competitive_bidding/non_leaping_michaels.summary:
Played instead of Leaping Michaels: over their preempt, a non-jump bid of a
new suit at the next level shows that suit and a major.

competitive_bidding/raptor.name: Raptor 1NT
competitive_bidding/raptor.summary:
An overcall of 1NT that shows a four-card major and a longer minor, rather
than a strong balanced hand.

competitive_bidding/responsive_doubles.name: Responsive Doubles
competitive_bidding/responsive_doubles.summary:
After partner doubles for takeout and the next player raises, advancer's
double is for takeout too, showing values and usually both unbid suits of a
kind (the majors or the minors).

competitive_bidding/rodrigue.name: Rodrigue
competitive_bidding/rodrigue.summary:
After partner's minor and their 1♠, a double shows four hearts, and five or
more hearts are shown by 2m with 8–10 points or 2♥ with 11 or more.

competitive_bidding/rosenkranz.name: Rosenkranz double
competitive_bidding/rosenkranz.summary:
When the opponents overcall partner's opening and advancer raises partner's
overcall, a double or redouble shows a top honour in partner's suit, and a
raise denies one.

competitive_bidding/rubensohl.name: Rubensohl
competitive_bidding/rubensohl.summary:
A transfer version of Lebensohl: after they overcall partner's 1NT,
responder's bids from 2NT up are transfers to the next suit, which lets
responder show a suit, a stopper or values at a lower level.

see.title: NT Bidding: Modern, Transfer, and Modern Transfer Lebensohl

competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt.name: Sandwich 1NT
competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt.summary:
In the sandwich seat, after the opponents have bid two suits, a 1NT overcall
shows the two unbid suits rather than a strong balanced hand.

competitive_bidding/scrambling_2nt.name: Scrambling 2NT
competitive_bidding/scrambling_2nt.summary:
In a competitive auction where a takeout double would be natural, advancer's
2NT asks partner to pick a minor or a two-suited contract, rather than
showing values.

competitive_bidding/snapdragon.name: Snapdragon doubles
competitive_bidding/snapdragon.summary:
When three suits have been bid, one by each of three players, fourth hand's
double shows the unbid suit and tolerance for partner's.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/sos_redouble.name: SOS redouble
competitive_bidding/sos_redouble.summary:
When a low-level contract is doubled for penalty, a redouble asks partner to
choose another suit, rather than showing strength.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/spear.name: Spear
competitive_bidding/spear.summary:
How to intervene after the opponents' 1♣ or 1♦ opening and 1NT response:
suit bids and double describe both-majors, one-major and strong hands.

competitive_bidding/suction.name: Suction
competitive_bidding/suction.summary:
Over their 1NT, each two-level suit bid shows either the next suit up or the
other two suits, so the overcall is ambiguous by design and partner bids the
next suit to find out.

competitive_bidding/support_cuebids.name: Support Cuebids
competitive_bidding/support_cuebids.summary:
A cue bid of the opponents' suit in response to partner's opening or
overcall shows a raise of partner's suit with limit-raise values or better,
leaving direct raises weaker.

see.title: Constructive Bidding Opposite 3rd Hand Openings: Cuebid as Limit Raise+ by a Passed Hand

competitive_bidding/support_doubles.name: Support Doubles and Redoubles
competitive_bidding/support_doubles.summary:
After opener's one-level opening and responder's one-level suit, when the
next player bids, opener's double shows exactly three-card support for
responder (a redouble after their double), and a raise shows four.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/takeout_doubles.name: Takeout Doubles
competitive_bidding/takeout_doubles.summary:
A double of an opening bid, when partner has not bid, asks partner to bid:
it shows opening values, shortness in their suit and support for the unbid
suits, or a hand too strong to overcall.

competitive_bidding/thrump_double.name: Thrump double
competitive_bidding/thrump_double.summary:
After partner opens and the opponents preempt at the three level,
responder's double asks opener to bid 3NT with a stopper, for a hand with
values and no fit or long suit.

competitive_bidding/transfer_advances.name: Transfer advances
competitive_bidding/transfer_advances.summary:
After partner's overcall, advancer's bids are transfers to the next suit, so
the overcaller can accept or show more, and advancer can describe more
hands.

competitive_bidding/unusual_vs_unusual.name: Unusual vs Unusual
competitive_bidding/unusual_vs_unusual.summary:
After they show two suits with Michaels or the Unusual 2NT, cue bids of
their suits show hands in the other two suits: one cue bid a raise of
partner, the other a strong hand in the fourth suit.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
Unusual vs. Unusual and Unusual vs. Michaels

defense/defensive_signals.name: Defensive Signals
defense/defensive_signals.summary:
Defenders' agreements on what their cards say: attitude (like this suit or
not), count (odd or even length) and suit preference (which other suit to
play), and which applies when.

defense/lavinthal.name: Lavinthal
defense/lavinthal.summary:
A discard is suit preference: a high card asks for the higher of the other
two suits, a low card for the lower.

defense/odd_even_discards.name: Odd-even discards
defense/odd_even_discards.summary:
A defender's first discard says something by being odd or even: an odd card
encourages that suit, an even card discourages and its size points to
another suit.

defense/opening_leads.name: Opening Leads
defense/opening_leads.summary:
The partnership's choice of card from each kind of holding on opening lead,
such as fourth best from length and the top of a sequence, so partner can
read the lead.

see.title: Fundamentals of Trick Taking – 4th Best Leads (Attitude)

defense/reverse_smith_echo.name: Reverse Smith echo
defense/reverse_smith_echo.summary:
Played instead of the Smith echo: on declarer's first suit, a defender's
high-low says they did not like partner's opening lead.

defense/rusinow_leads.name: Rusinow leads
defense/rusinow_leads.summary:
Played instead of standard honour leads: from touching honours lead the
second highest (the king from KQ, the queen from QJ), usually only at trick
one against suit contracts.

defense/smith_echo.name: Smith echo
defense/smith_echo.summary:
On declarer's first suit, a defender's high-low says whether they liked
partner's opening lead, rather than giving count.

defense/upside_down_signals.name: Upside-down signals
defense/upside_down_signals.summary:
Played instead of standard signals: a low card encourages and a high one
discourages, and count is shown upside down too, so the defenders keep their
high cards.

see.title: Defensive Carding: Upside-Down Count and Attitude (UDCA)
